chunks: As for what Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Ṣafwān, from ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said:

Indeed, in the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام, if a man performs the obligatory tawaf of the House in eight circuits and is certain of eight, he adds six to it. Likewise, if he is certain that he has performed eight circuits of saʿy, he adds six to it.

So the proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it as applying to one who did that forgetfully, according to what we have previously stated; and along with that, when he has performed eight circuits of saʿy, he is at al-Ṣafā.

But if he knows that he has performed eight circuits while he is at al-Marwah, then repetition becomes obligatory upon him in every case, because that would mean he began with al-Marwah; and it is not permissible for one who did that to build upon it. And that which indicates this is:

key_terms.أَشْوَاطٍ: circuits or rounds in tawaf or saʿy
key_terms.الْإِعَادَةُ: repetition of the act due to invalidity
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the other endpoint of saʿy
key_terms.سَعَى: performed saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah
key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: the written source attributed to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام cited as authority

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone performs eight circuits in saʿy or tawaf during hajj?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal ruling for one who exceeds seven circuits in tawaf or saʿy during hajj rites. It distinguishes between a case of forgetfulness that may be completed in a certain way and a case showing that the rite was begun incorrectly, in which case repetition is required.
